name: Eye Saccade Analysis
description: Detects unnatural saccadic eye movement patterns — AI videos often lack realistic micro-saccades (Duchowski, 2017).
mechanism:
This method analyzes saccadic eye movements for deepfake detection:

1. **Saccade Detection**: Saccades (rapid ballistic eye movements) are detected from the gaze direction temporal signal. Saccades are characterized by their amplitude (typical 1-40°), peak velocity (up to 500°/s), and duration (20-200ms).

2. **Main Sequence Verification**: Saccades follow the "main sequence" — a fixed relationship between amplitude and peak velocity: V_peak ∝ √amplitude (Bahill et al., 1975). The method checks whether detected saccades conform to this physiological invariant. AI-generated eye movements may violate the main sequence — producing incorrect velocity-amplitude relationships.

3. **Saccade Dynamics Analysis**: Natural saccades have characteristic dynamics: rapid acceleration, smooth velocity profile with single peak, small post-saccadic oscillation. The method analyzes each saccade's kinematic profile. AI-generated saccades may show: multiple velocity peaks, incorrect acceleration/deceleration asymmetry, or missing post-saccadic ringing.

4. **Fixation-Saccade Pattern**: Natural gaze alternates between fixations (~200-400ms, stable gaze) and saccades (~20-80ms, rapid shifts). The method verifies this pattern — particularly the fixation duration distribution (approximately log-normal) and saccade rate (3-4 per second during reading/scanning). Deepfakes may show anomalous fixation-saccade patterns.

5. **Bilateral Saccade Coordination**: Both eyes execute saccades simultaneously (conjugate movements). The method checks saccade synchrony between eyes — independent AI generation of each eye may produce asynchronous or differently-sized saccades between left and right eyes.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
